Key Takeaways


##


1. Halloween puns: Believe it or not, they’re important for small business owners. Puns, slogans, and taglines might make some roll their eyes, but they also increase brand awareness and give people a catchphrase to remember your business.
2. A good Halloween pun can emphasize a deal you’re promoting or make a marketing campaign more memorable. It can also help you relate to your customer base and make your advertisements more personable.

## Halloween Puns, Slogan, & Taglines From Real Companies


Let’s break down some real examples of Halloween puns, slogans, and taglines and discuss how you can create something similar as a small business owner.


1. “Happy Halloween: Spooky Savings Inside” – **Cheerble** : Cheerble sent me this message promoting its Halloween deals. I like how simple it is, and it makes me curious about the offer inside the email.
2. “Grab your gear, and let’s get to carving. 🎃” – : This tagline was used in a[social media post for Caterpillar](https://www.facebook.com/caterpillarinc/videos/happy-halloween/2311831358968979/) . It speaks directly to the brand’s customers and draws attention to its products.
3. “Tricked and defeated” – **Yahoo** : Yahoo sent me this[email subject line](https://www.thryv.com/blog/email-subject-lines/) last Halloween after I lost in fantasy football. It was timely and relevant to the last product that I used from them.
4. “No Tricks Just a Spooky Good Deal!🎃” – : Try the World is an ecommerce brand that relies on email for[customer communication](https://www.thryv.com/blog/customer-communication-struggles/) . I like how this slogan uses an emoji to make the message more festive.
5. “Boo! The ‘90s are BACK.👻” – : This slogan grabs your attention immediately with the exclamation at the beginning. The capitalization emphasizes that there are new products in stock.
6. “Sweet, soft styles that’ll put a spell on you.” – **Bombas** : Here’s a good example of a Halloween marketing slogan. Notice how it’s specific to a product line, not the company as a whole.
7. “Enjoy autumn in all of its spectacular glory!🍁” – : This tagline made our list because it wasn’t Halloween-centric. It’s a good reminder that[fall marketing slogans](https://www.thryv.com/blog/fall-marketing-slogans/) can be as effective as Halloween.
8. “We’ve got the treats 🎃 All you need to do is click ➡️” – ’: This slogan from Dunkin’ plays off Halloween and its product line. When this brand uses the word “treats,” it immediately makes you think of pastries, doughnuts, and other breakfast sweets.
9. “Hey Google, let’s play a game.” – **Google** : This email steals a line from a popular horror movie called “Saw.” Pop culture references like this are often a great way to grab people’s attention.
10. “Deals you can sink your teeth into.” – **Smokey Bones** : This slogan is effective because it’s advertising a local food chain. “Sinking your teeth” is a reference to Halloween, but it also makes you think about getting a good meal, too.
11. “Trick or treat and treat and treat and treat….” – **John Deere** : This Halloween marketing pun accompanied a[video](https://www.facebook.com/JohnDeereUSCA/videos/a-john-deere-sized-halloween/857192299399944/) of a tractor towing a truckload of candy. It’s simple and does a great job of complementing the brand’s video.

## Tagline Best Practices: Test, Trust, and Turn Them into Campaign Gold


### 1. Choose a handful of taglines and A/B test them


Rather than selecting one favorite tagline and running with it, treat them like hypotheses:


- Pick **2–4 taglines** that align with your brand voice (e.g. “Don’t ghost us — shop today!” vs. “Spook-tacular savings this fall!”)
- Use **Thryv Marketing Automation** to send parallel email campaigns (or drip messages) with alternating taglines.
- Track which version yields higher opens, click-throughs, or conversions.


You can also test within social media captions (if your plan supports post variants), but email is usually the easiest to control. Over a few days, you’ll see which tagline resonates most with real audiences.


***Pro tip:*** Use a 20–40% traffic split for your test groups initially (e.g. 30% to version A, 30% to B, reserve the rest for the “winner” version going forward).


Once you identify the winning variant, shift your full campaign to that top performer.


### 2. Leverage reputation-driven messaging to bolster credibility


A fun tagline alone is great — but when paired with social proof, it becomes a trust signal. Here’s how to combine the two:


- In your email footer or within the message, pair a tagline with a real customer testimonial.
*“Don’t ghost us — shop today! (Because our customers say they never want to leave…)”* ** Or even embed a one-line quote under the tagline.
- In social or paid ad creative, overlay the tagline on the image alongside a short review snippet or star rating (“Scare away your problems — 4.9★ average review”).
- Use[Thryv’s Automated Reviews](https://www.thryv.com/features/automated-reviews/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) functionality to surface your top-rated reviews or quotes. Automatically request reviews, and then syndicate best ones into your marketing channels.


By coupling playful messaging with real voices, you reinforce both brand personality and trustworthiness.


### 3. Turn winning taglines into campaign assets


Once your A/B test reveals the most effective tagline, don’t leave it static in emails — turn it into visual assets. Use[Thryv Website Builder](https://www.thryv.com/features/professional-website/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) ,[Social Media Management](https://www.thryv.com/features/social-media/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) , and landing page tools to amplify it:


- Design a **branded graphic or banner** for your homepage or landing page with the tagline, spooky visuals, and a CTA.
- Use it as a **social media post or story image** (vertical & square versions), ideally pre-scheduled via Thryv’s Social tools.
- Create matching **ad creative** (if running paid campaigns), using the same tagline + visual style for unity.
- Use the tagline in **landing page headers** , hero sections, or popups during the Halloween period.


This ensures your tagline becomes a consistent “thread” across email, site, and social — reinforcing message recall and engagement.


### 4. Operational flow summary (inside Thryv)


Here’s a sample workflow you (or your marketing team) could execute inside Thryv:


1. **Brainstorm variants** — pick 3 tagline candidates from your list or custom ones.
2. **Set up A/B sends** — use automated drip or campaign sends via Marketing Automation, splitting recipients.
3. **Measure performance** — open rate, clicks, conversions. Let data decide the winner.
4. **Activate the winner across channels** — swap in the winning tagline for all remaining emails, social posts, and site banners.
5. **Pull in review content** — via Automated Reviews, tag your top reviews and insert them into email footers, social graphics, site sidebars.
6. **Monitor and iterate** — if one tagline works extremely better, consider a fresh test mid-campaign (e.g. “Our trick is treating customers” vs. “Scare away your problems with \[Brand\]”).
7. **Report results** — track lift in open rates, click-throughs, conversions, social engagement, and review acquisition.


## Marketing Your Business During Spooky Season


Whether you’re promoting a new product, announcing a special deal, or just trying to boost brand awareness, a good tagline or slogan can make or break a[seasonal marketing campaign](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-seasonal-marketing/) .


Make yours memorable by adapting one of the slogans above. Or, create one from scratch using inspiration from our examples. Either way, ensure your messages are on-brand and easy to remember, and you’ll be well on your way to creating a successful Halloween marketing campaign.
